name: Plank
form_cues: Stack elbows under shoulders and push the floor away
Squeeze glutes and brace like you're about to be poked
Keep one straight line from head to heels
common_mistakes: Hips piked high to make it easier
safety: Stop if you feel it in your lower back rather than your abs.
notes: Quality beats time: end the set when your hips start to drop.

name: High plank
form_cues: Hands under shoulders, arms straight but not locked
Spread your fingers and push the floor away
Tuck pelvis slightly and keep a straight line
safety: Go to fists or forearms if your wrists hurt.

name: Side plank
form_cues: Elbow directly under shoulder, feet stacked or staggered
Lift hips so ankles, hips and shoulders line up
Push the floor away and don't let the top hip roll back
common_mistakes: Shoulder shrugged up to the ear
safety: Bend the bottom knee to shorten the lever if your shoulder complains.
notes: Stagger the feet for more stability; stack them for more challenge.

name: Side plank hip dips
form_cues: Start in a strong side plank on your forearm
Lower the hip a few centimetres toward the floor
Drive it back up past level and pause
common_mistakes: Rushing and bouncing the hip off the floor
Twisting the torso instead of moving sideways
safety: Keep the shoulder packed down; stop if it pinches.

name: Side plank with rotation
form_cues: Hold a tall side plank with the top arm reaching to the ceiling
Rotate and thread the top arm under your body
Return slowly without letting the hips drop
progressions: Side plank with a light dumbbell reach-through
safety: Keep the supporting shoulder stacked over the elbow.

name: Copenhagen plank
form_cues: Top leg rests on a bench or chair, bottom leg hangs free
Lift hips into a straight side plank line
Squeeze the top leg down into the bench the whole time
common_mistakes: Too much leg on the bench too soon
safety: Start with the knee on the bench to protect the groin; stop with sharp adductor pain.
notes: Great for groin injury prevention in field sports. A chair works if you have no bench.

name: Reverse plank
form_cues: Sit with legs long, hands behind hips, fingers toward feet
Drive hips up until your body is one straight line
Squeeze glutes and keep the chin neutral
safety: Do it on forearms if your wrists or shoulders object.

name: Bear plank hold
form_cues: On hands and knees, hands under shoulders, knees under hips
Lift knees about 3 cm off the floor
Keep your back flat like a table
safety: Keep breathing; go to fists if wrists hurt.

name: Plank shoulder taps
form_cues: Start in a high plank with feet a bit wider than hips
Tap the opposite shoulder with one hand at a time
Keep the hips still, like a glass of water is on your back
safety: Widen your feet if you can't stop the hips rocking.

name: Plank up-down
form_cues: Start on forearms in a plank
Press up to hands one arm at a time, then lower back down
Alternate the leading arm and keep the hips level
safety: Widen the feet for stability; skip if you have wrist pain.

name: Spiderman plank
form_cues: Start in a forearm or high plank
Bring one knee out to the same-side elbow
Return the leg with control and switch sides
safety: Move slowly; it is a strength drill, not cardio.

name: Body saw
form_cues: Forearm plank with feet on sliders or a towel
Push your body back so elbows go in front of your face
Pull back to the start without letting hips sag
common_mistakes: Lower back arching as you push back
safety: Only go as far as you can keep the ribs down.
notes: A towel on a hard floor or socks on wood work as sliders.

name: Crunch
form_cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat
Curl your ribs toward your hips until shoulder blades lift
Lower slowly and keep a fist-sized gap under the chin
common_mistakes: Lifting the whole back off the floor (that's a sit-up)
safety: Support the head lightly with fingertips; don't pull.
notes: Hold a plate on the chest to add load.

name: Bicycle crunch
form_cues: Hands lightly behind the head, shoulders off the floor
Rotate one shoulder toward the opposite knee as the other leg extends
Slow down and pause on each twist
common_mistakes: Flapping elbows instead of rotating the ribs
safety: Keep the extended leg higher if your back arches.

name: Reverse crunch
form_cues: Lie down, knees bent at 90°, hands by your sides
Curl your hips off the floor toward your ribs
Lower slowly without the feet crashing down
common_mistakes: Only moving the legs, not the pelvis
safety: Keep it slow to protect the lower back.

name: Oblique crunch
form_cues: Lie on your back with one ankle on the other knee
Curl and rotate the opposite shoulder toward the raised knee
Lower slowly and finish all reps before switching
safety: Keep the movement small and controlled.

name: Heel touches
form_cues: Lie with knees bent, feet a bit wider than hips
Lift shoulders and reach one hand to the same-side heel
Stay curled up as you tap side to side
common_mistakes: Pulling the chin into the chest
safety: Fine for most people; rest the head between sets if the neck tires.

name: Toe touch crunch
form_cues: Lie down with legs pointing to the ceiling
Reach your hands toward your toes, lifting shoulder blades
Lower slowly and keep the legs still
common_mistakes: Throwing the arms instead of curling the trunk
safety: Bend the knees slightly if your hamstrings are tight.

name: Sit-up
form_cues: Knees bent, feet flat, arms crossed on chest
Curl up one vertebra at a time until you're upright
Lower with control rather than flopping back
common_mistakes: Jerking up with the arms or neck
safety: Skip or swap for crunches if sit-ups aggravate a disc problem.
notes: Anchor the feet under a sofa if needed.

name: Butterfly sit-up
form_cues: Soles of feet together, knees out wide
Reach arms overhead and swing up to touch your feet
Roll back down and touch the floor behind you
safety: Use a rolled towel under the lower back if it feels uncomfortable.
notes: Common in CrossFit; the knees-out position limits hip flexor pull.

name: Lying leg raise
form_cues: Lie flat, hands under hips or by your sides
Press the lower back into the floor and raise straight legs to vertical
Lower slowly until just before the back lifts
common_mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor
safety: Bend the knees or shorten the range if your lower back lifts.

name: Flutter kicks
form_cues: Lie down, hands under hips, lower back pressed down
Lift legs a few centimetres off the floor
Kick small, quick up-and-down alternations
safety: Raise the legs higher if your back arches.
notes: Can also be tracked as time (30–45 sec).

name: Scissor kicks
form_cues: Lie down, lower back pressed into the floor
Hold legs just off the floor
Cross one leg over the other, then switch, keeping legs straight
safety: Keep the legs higher to make it easier on the back.

name: Dead bug
form_cues: Lie on your back, arms to ceiling, knees at 90°
Lower the opposite arm and leg toward the floor
Keep the lower back flat and breathe out as you reach
safety: A good choice for sensitive backs; shorten the range if the back lifts.
notes: Hold a dumbbell or press into a band to progress.

name: Bird dog
form_cues: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat
Reach the opposite arm and leg out long
Pause for 2 seconds without the hips tilting, then switch
common_mistakes: Arching the back as the leg lifts
regressions: Bird dog arm or leg only
safety: Keep it small and controlled if you have back pain.
notes: One of McGill's 'Big 3' back-health moves.

name: Hollow body hold
form_cues: Press your lower back into the floor
Lift shoulders and legs, arms reaching past your ears
Hold the banana shape and keep breathing
common_mistakes: Lower back lifting off the floor
safety: Tuck the knees or bring arms forward if your back lifts.
notes: A foundation for gymnastics and calisthenics skills.

name: Hollow body rock
form_cues: Get into a tight hollow hold
Rock from shoulders to hips without changing shape
Keep arms by the ears and legs together
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips to make the rock
safety: Only rock if you can hold the hollow position for 30 sec first.

name: V-up
form_cues: Lie flat with arms overhead and legs straight
Lift arms and legs together to meet over your hips
Lower slowly back to a hovering hollow position
safety: Build up through tuck-ups if your back arches.

name: Tuck-up
form_cues: Lie flat with arms overhead
Sit up as you pull your knees to your chest
Hug the shins briefly, then lower with control
safety: Keep the motion controlled to protect the lower back.

name: Jackknife sit-up
form_cues: Lie flat, arms overhead
Raise one straight leg as you reach both hands to that foot
Lower back down and alternate legs
common_mistakes: Bending the reaching leg a lot
safety: Keep the non-working leg on the floor for support.

name: Seated knee tuck
form_cues: Sit leaning back on your hands, feet off the floor
Pull your knees toward your chest as your chest moves toward them
Extend the legs out long without touching the floor
safety: Lean back on forearms if you feel it in your lower back.
notes: Can also be done on a bench edge.

name: V-sit hold
form_cues: Sit tall and lean back slightly
Lift your legs to make a V with your body
Keep the chest open and spine long
safety: Bend the knees if you can't keep your back straight.
notes: Yoga's boat pose is a similar shape.

name: Russian twist
equipment: Optional plate, dumbbell or medicine ball
form_cues: Sit leaning back about 45° with a tall chest
Turn your shoulders, not just your arms, side to side
Lift the feet for a harder version
common_mistakes: Swinging the arms while the torso stays still
safety: Skip with disc problems that dislike loaded twisting.
notes: Add a medicine ball, plate or dumbbell for load.

name: Mountain climbers
form_cues: Start in a high plank, hands under shoulders
Drive one knee toward your chest, then switch quickly
Keep the hips level and shoulders over the hands
regressions: Incline mountain climbers on a bench
safety: Slow down if your wrists or lower back complain.
notes: Track as time (30–45 sec) for conditioning work.

name: Cross-body mountain climber
form_cues: Start in a strong high plank
Drive each knee toward the opposite elbow
Keep the hips low and shoulders still
safety: Keep the pace controlled if your back sags.

name: Lying windshield wipers
form_cues: Lie on your back with arms out in a T, legs up at 90°
Lower your legs to one side while shoulders stay down
Pull them back to centre and go to the other side
safety: Bend the knees to shorten the lever if your back aches.

name: Stomach vacuum
form_cues: Breathe out fully through your mouth
Pull your belly button in toward your spine
Hold while taking small, shallow breaths
common_mistakes: Sucking in the chest instead of the belly
safety: Avoid if you are pregnant or have high blood pressure.
notes: Popular in physique and rehab circles for deep-core awareness.

name: Single-leg stand
form_cues: Stand tall and lift one foot just off the floor
Spread your toes and keep a slight bend in the standing knee
Fix your eyes on a point ahead
common_mistakes: Hip dropping on the lifted side
safety: Stand near a wall or counter in case you lose balance.
notes: Great for ankle sprain rehab and fall prevention.

name: Single-leg stand, eyes closed
form_cues: Get steady on one leg with eyes open first
Close your eyes and keep the standing knee soft
Let the ankle make small corrections
safety: Always do this next to a wall or sturdy support.
notes: Removing vision makes the ankle and inner ear work harder.

name: Tandem stance hold
form_cues: Place one heel directly in front of the other foot's toes
Stand tall with arms relaxed
Hold, then switch which foot is in front
safety: Stand in a corner or by a counter for safety.
notes: Common in falls-prevention programmes for older adults.

name: Heel-to-toe walk
form_cues: Walk in a straight line, heel touching the toes of the back foot
Keep your eyes forward, not on your feet
Move slowly and steadily
safety: Walk beside a wall or counter until confident.

name: Star excursion balance
form_cues: Balance on one leg in a quarter squat
Reach the free toe as far as you can along each direction like a clock
Tap lightly, return to the centre and keep the standing heel down
common_mistakes: Putting weight on the reaching foot
safety: Keep reaches within a range you can control.
notes: Used by physios to test and train ankle and knee stability.

name: Y-balance reach
form_cues: Stand on one leg at the centre of a Y
Reach the free foot forward, then back-left, then back-right
Touch lightly and return without losing balance
common_mistakes: Leaning heavily on the reaching foot
safety: Mark the lines with tape; stay near support if needed.
notes: Compare reach distances side to side to spot imbalances.

name: Single-leg toe touch
form_cues: Stand on one leg with a soft knee
Hinge forward and reach your hand toward the floor
Squeeze the glute to stand back up tall
safety: Reach to a box or chair if the floor is too far.

name: Single-leg airplane
form_cues: Hinge forward on one leg until your torso is near horizontal
Rotate your pelvis open toward the ceiling
Rotate back down so hips face the floor, staying balanced
common_mistakes: Rotating the shoulders instead of the hips
Losing the hinge and standing up
safety: Hold a wall or rack with one hand until you've mastered it.
notes: Builds hip control for running and lifting.

name: Ab wheel rollout
form_cues: Kneel and hold the wheel under your shoulders
Roll forward with ribs down and glutes squeezed
Pull back with your abs, not by sitting the hips back
common_mistakes: Lower back sagging at the bottom
Going further than you can control
safety: Use a short range to start; stop if you feel your lower back.
notes: Roll toward a wall to cap the range while learning.

name: Standing ab wheel rollout
form_cues: From standing, fold and place the wheel on the floor
Roll out to full extension with a hollow body
Pull back up to a pike without the back arching
common_mistakes: Bending the knees to cheat back up
safety: Master 15+ kneeling rollouts first; very demanding on the lower back.

name: Hanging leg raise
form_cues: Hang with active shoulders and legs together
Raise straight legs to hip height or higher by curling the pelvis
Lower slowly without swinging
common_mistakes: Only lifting with hip flexors, no pelvic curl
safety: Use ab straps if grip or shoulders give out first.

name: Hanging knee raise
form_cues: Hang from the bar with shoulders engaged
Bring knees up toward the chest, curling the hips
Lower under control and stop the swing
safety: Use ab straps if your grip fails before your abs.

name: Toes-to-bar
form_cues: Hang with a shoulder-width grip and press the bar down
Lift straight legs until your toes touch the bar
Lower with control between reps (or kip if training CrossFit style)
safety: Warm up the shoulders and hamstrings first.
notes: Strict and kipping versions exist; kipping is for conditioning.

name: Hanging windshield wipers
form_cues: Hang and raise straight legs up to the bar
Rotate the legs side to side like a wiper
Keep the upper body still and controlled
safety: Only attempt once strict toes-to-bar feel easy.

name: Dumbbell side bend
form_cues: Stand tall with one dumbbell at your side
Bend sideways toward the weight, keeping hips still
Pull back up with the opposite obliques
common_mistakes: Holding weights in both hands (they cancel out)
safety: Move slowly; avoid with lower back pain on side bending.

name: Suitcase carry
form_cues: Hold a heavy weight in one hand by your side
Walk tall without leaning toward or away from it
Take short, steady steps and keep the shoulders level
safety: Set the weight down with a flat back, bending the knees.
notes: Track distance in the reps field; works for anti-lateral flexion.

name: Waiter's carry
form_cues: Press a weight overhead and lock the arm by your ear
Brace and walk tall with ribs down
Keep the bicep near the ear the whole walk
safety: Only go overhead if your shoulder has pain-free mobility.

name: Plank pull-through
form_cues: High plank with a weight beside your ribs
Reach under with the opposite hand and drag it across
Keep the hips square and still
safety: Use a light weight first; widen the feet for stability.

name: Kettlebell windmill
form_cues: Press the bell overhead and turn your feet away from it
Push the hips out and hinge down to touch the floor
Keep eyes on the bell and arm locked the whole time
common_mistakes: Rounding the spine instead of hinging
safety: Learn it with no weight; stop if the shoulder feels unstable.

name: Band Pallof press
form_cues: Anchor a band at chest height and stand side-on
Press the band straight out from your chest
Resist the twist, pause, then bring it back
safety: Check the anchor is secure before loading the band.
notes: Kneeling or split stance versions shift the challenge.

name: Band woodchop
form_cues: Anchor the band high and stand side-on
Pull diagonally across your body to the opposite hip
Pivot the back foot and rotate through the trunk
safety: Use a band you can control on the way back.

name: Medicine ball woodchop
form_cues: Hold the ball high over one shoulder
Chop down diagonally to the outside of the opposite knee
Squat a little and pivot the back foot as you rotate
common_mistakes: Releasing the ball (this is not a throw)
safety: Keep the back long as you squat down.
notes: A dumbbell held by the ends works too.

name: Stability ball crunch
form_cues: Sit then walk out until the ball is under your mid-back
Let the back stretch over the ball, then curl up
Lower slowly back into the stretch
common_mistakes: Rolling the ball rather than curling
safety: Keep feet wide for stability.
notes: The ball allows a bigger range than a floor crunch.

name: Stability ball rollout
form_cues: Kneel with forearms on the ball
Roll it forward as your body straightens
Pull it back with your abs, keeping ribs down
safety: Stop the roll before your back starts to arch.

name: Stir the pot
form_cues: Hold a forearm plank on the ball
Draw small circles with your elbows
Keep the hips and lower back totally still
progressions: Stir the pot with feet together
safety: Keep circles small; stop if the lower back sags.
notes: Popularised by Dr. Stuart McGill for spine-friendly core work.

name: Stability ball plank
form_cues: Place forearms on the ball, legs straight behind
Brace hard so the ball doesn't wobble
Keep a straight line from head to heels
safety: Put the ball against a wall the first few times.

name: Stability ball pike
form_cues: Start in a push-up position with shins on the ball
Lift your hips high, rolling the ball to your toes
Lower with control back to a flat plank
safety: Keep shoulders over hands; strong wrists required.

name: Stability ball knee tuck
form_cues: Start in a push-up position with shins on the ball
Pull your knees toward your chest, rolling the ball in
Push it back to a straight plank without sagging
safety: Keep the ball close to start; further out is harder.

name: Stability ball pass
form_cues: Lie flat holding the ball overhead
Lift arms and legs to pass the ball to your feet
Lower both, then bring it back to your hands
safety: Don't lower your legs further than you can keep the back flat.

name: Stability ball seated balance
form_cues: Sit tall on the ball, feet hip-width, knees at 90°
Lift one foot slightly off the floor and hold
Switch feet without wobbling; progress to marching
safety: Use a ball sized so your hips are level with your knees.

name: Stability ball kneeling balance
form_cues: Start with hands and knees on the ball beside a wall
Lift your hands off and kneel upright
Keep hips forward and eyes on a fixed point
safety: Clear the area and use a wall or partner nearby; falls are possible.

name: BOSU single-leg balance
form_cues: Step onto the centre of the dome with one foot
Keep a soft knee and lift the other foot
Look ahead and let the ankle make small corrections
safety: Start next to a wall or rack for support.
notes: A foam balance pad is a good alternative.

name: BOSU squat
form_cues: Stand on the dome with feet hip-width
Sit back into a squat with knees tracking over toes
Stand back up without wobbling
common_mistakes: Going too deep and losing balance
progressions: BOSU squat on the flat side (dome down)
safety: Use the dome side up; standing on the flat side is advanced.

name: BOSU plank
form_cues: Forearms on the dome, legs straight behind you
Brace and squeeze glutes to hold a straight line
Keep the platform still and breathe
progressions: BOSU plank with feet on dome
safety: Hold the edges if forearms slip.

name: BOSU crunch
form_cues: Sit with the dome under your lower back
Lean back into the stretch, then curl up
Lower slowly and keep feet planted
safety: Keep feet wide to stay stable.

name: Dragon flag
form_cues: Lie on a bench and grip it behind your head
Lift your body to vertical, resting on the upper back
Lower as one straight line, then raise back up
common_mistakes: Lower back arching on the way down
safety: Very demanding; build up with negatives and stop if your neck takes the load.

name: Bench leg raise
form_cues: Lie on a bench gripping it behind your head
Raise your legs and curl the hips off the bench
Lower slowly past bench level without arching
safety: Bend the knees if your lower back arches.

name: Decline sit-up
form_cues: Hook feet under the pads, arms crossed on chest
Curl up until your torso is near vertical
Lower slowly to just above the bench
safety: Lower the bench angle to make it easier.
notes: Hold a plate on your chest to add load.

name: Decline crunch
form_cues: Secure your feet and lie back on the decline bench
Curl your shoulders up without sitting all the way
Lower with control, keeping tension
safety: Start at a shallow angle.

name: Cable rope crunch
form_cues: Kneel facing the stack, rope beside your head
Curl your ribs toward your hips, rounding the spine
Keep the hips still and return slowly
common_mistakes: Sitting back with the hips instead of crunching
safety: Keep the weight moderate so you can feel the abs, not the hips.
notes: One of the best ways to load the abs progressively.

name: Cable woodchop
form_cues: Set the pulley high and stand side-on
Pull diagonally down across your body to the opposite hip
Rotate through the torso and pivot the back foot
safety: Use a load you can control on the way back up.

name: Low-to-high cable woodchop
form_cues: Set the pulley low and stand side-on
Pull up diagonally across your body to above the opposite shoulder
Drive from the hips and keep arms long
safety: Keep the spine long; don't round to grab the handle.

name: Pallof press
form_cues: Stand side-on with the handle at chest
Press it straight out and resist the pull
Hold 2 seconds, then bring it back slowly
safety: Start light; it's harder than it looks.

name: Standing cable rotation
form_cues: Set the pulley at chest height, stand side-on
Rotate away from the stack with arms straight
Return slowly without letting it yank you back
common_mistakes: Hips locked so the lower back twists
safety: Let the hips turn a little to spare the lower back.

name: Landmine rotation
form_cues: Hold the bar end at arm's length above your head
Rotate it down in an arc to one hip, pivoting the feet
Bring it back over the top and go to the other side
common_mistakes: Twisting from the lower back with locked hips
safety: Start with the empty bar; use a corner if you have no landmine.

name: Barbell rollout
form_cues: Load small round plates and kneel behind the bar
Roll forward with ribs down and glutes tight
Pull back with your abs
safety: Use plates with round edges so the bar rolls smoothly.
notes: Wider grip than an ab wheel; good gym substitute.

name: Suspension pike
form_cues: Feet in the straps, start in a high plank
Lift hips high keeping legs straight
Lower slowly back to a flat plank
safety: Keep shoulders stacked over hands.

name: Suspension knee tuck
form_cues: Feet in the straps, high plank position
Pull knees in toward your chest
Extend back to a straight plank
safety: Keep the straps at mid-calf height.

name: Suspension fallout
form_cues: Hold handles facing away from the anchor, body leaning forward
Let arms rise overhead as you fall forward
Pull back up with your abs, not the arms
safety: A steeper body angle is harder; start more upright.

name: Ab crunch machine
form_cues: Set the seat so the pads sit on your chest or shoulders
Curl down by bringing ribs to hips
Return slowly without letting the stack slam
common_mistakes: Using too much weight and hip-flexing
safety: Start light and keep the motion in the abs.

name: Rotary torso machine
form_cues: Sit tall with legs locked in
Rotate through your trunk, not your arms
Return slowly to centre
safety: Use a moderate load; avoid with disc issues aggravated by twisting.

name: Captain's chair knee raise
form_cues: Back against the pad, forearms on the rests
Lift knees to chest by curling the hips up
Lower with control without swinging
common_mistakes: Only lifting to 90° without curling the pelvis
safety: Keep shoulders down, not shrugged.
notes: Straighten the legs for a harder leg raise version.

name: GHD sit-up
form_cues: Sit on the pad with feet locked, hips just past it
Lower back to parallel, then reach behind if trained
Kick the knees straight to sit up and reach for your feet
common_mistakes: Going too far back too soon
Doing high volume on the first try
safety: Start with low reps and a short range; overuse can cause rhabdo or back strain.

name: 45-degree side bend
form_cues: Lie sideways on the bench, hip on the pad, feet locked
Lower your torso sideways toward the floor
Raise back up past level using the top-side obliques
safety: Use a short range first; stop with sharp back pain.
